 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And
227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To Directing
The R-5 To Consider The Applications Filed By The
Petitioner For Issue Of No Objection Certificate To Run
The Bio Diesel (B100) Vide Annx-T.
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing,
This Day, Order  WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER The petitioner asserts that he has been operating a Bio-Diesel bunk under the name and style of M/s. DNV Filling Station since 2018 at Sy. No. 45/5, measuring 20 guntas, situated at Panthanahalli Village, Kyasamballi Hobli, K.G.F. Taluk, Kolar District, after obtaining the necessary license/permissions from the competent authority. 
2. Under the given circumstances, the first respondent suspended the sale of Bio-Diesel, citing that the petitioner had not obtained a license, among other reasons. 
3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
4. The Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), Government of India, issued a communication dated 1.12.2014, NC: 2024:KHC:38574 stating that methyl ester is not a petroleum product and does not fall under the provisions of the Petroleum Rules, 2002.
Sri. Dileep. D. N vs The Union Of India on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157764562/
2 5. Respondents No. 1 and 2 have also filed a statement of objections, stating that Bio-Diesel/methyl ester does not come under the purview of petroleum products and, therefore, does not attract the provisions of the Petroleum Rules, 2002. As a result, suspending the sale of Bio-Diesel on the grounds that the petitioner has not obtained permission is legally unsustainable. Furthermore, the first respondent lacks the authority to suspend the sale of Bio-Diesel when it does not fall under the purview of petroleum products, and the Petroleum Rules, 2002, do not apply. Therefore, the impugned cancellation/suspension of Bio-Diesel sales lacks authority and is not legally sustainable. 
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. 
7. The impugned letter/notice dated 5.4.2022, issued by the first respondent, vide Annexure-S, and the impugned endorsement dated 7.5.2022, issued by the fifth respondent, vide Annexure-X, are hereby quashed. 
8. The petitioner is at liberty to sell Bio-Diesel in accordance with the law. 
Sd/-
(HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR) JUDGE HR Sri. Dileep. D. N vs The Union Of India on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157764562/
